title: Ship status document (ship-ctl status --json, version 1)
description: Produced by ship-ctl on the Ship (W5); consumed by FleetLedger (W8, W10) and ship-axi (W7, via /run/shipshape/status.json). Holds state and account names, never tokens. See contracts/ship-ctl.md.

tooling.description: Version of the installed Ship tooling bundle (bundle.json tooling_version).

state.description: provisioning: cloud-init or ship-provision not finished. needs-sign-in: Claude not signed in. ready: signed in, herdr up, no agents. running: one or more agents.

attention.description: Things a person should look at. Empty when all is well.

code.description: Codes the Ship emits: agent-waiting, signin-missing, signin-expiring, signin-expired, unit-failed, reboot-required, herdr-restart-pending, core-restart-pending, tmp-reboot-pending, provision-failed, tool-waiting, tool-failed, agent-repo-waiting, agent-repo-failed, host-cert-expiring, host-cert-expired, net-collector-down, overlay-down, agent-relaunch-failed, agents-share-folder (advice: two live Claude agents or more work in one folder, subject the folder; not when each is an [[autostart]] entry for it), autostart-folder-taken (an [[autostart]] agent not running is not started afresh while another agent the record keeps running works in its folder; subject the entry), runtime-switch-failed, runtime-switch-unfinished, runtime-deprecated (the Ship runs classic herdr, which the next release removes; the message names the command that moves it). FleetLedger adds its own (signin-wrong-account, behind-tooling, tags-differ, host-cert-missing, ssh-trust-behind) when it displays a Ship. Consumers show unknown codes as-is.

subject.description: What it is about: an agent name, service id, unit or tool id.

tmp.description: Where /tmp lives. fs: now (tmpfs: in memory; disk: a folder on the root disk; unknown: the mount table could not be read). next_boot: what it is from the next boot (disk once ship-provision has masked tmp.mount). Absent from Ships with older tooling.

herdr.description: What runs the agents: herdr's server, or herdr-core on a Ship with ship.toml runtime = "core" (runtime says which).

runtime.description: herdr: the herdr server (herdr --version, herdr agent list). core: herdr-core (hc --version, hc ls and hc get), whose agents report their own state. Absent from Ships with older tooling: herdr.

name.description: herdr agent name, if it has one (ShipShape names every agent it records).

mode.description: Claude permission mode from the mode ledger, else the agent record's; null if unknown or not Claude.

pane.description: herdr pane id, e.g. w1:p2; on herdr-core the terminal's address, e.g. t3.

workspace.description: On herdr-core the terminal's herdr.space label (shipshape for the agents ShipShape starts).

blocked_kind.description: herdr-core, while blocked: what the agent waits for, in its own word (permission, question, auth).

message.description: herdr-core, while blocked: what the agent says it waits for (e.g. the command to approve, or the question).

method.description: api-fallback: ship-ctl started the recorded agents again through herdr's API (agent_record.resume says the same, as ship-ctl). hidden-client: ship-resume let herdr resume them (tooling before the agent record).

auth.description: One entry per sign-in service. Known ids: claude, gcloud, gcloud_adc, github. More may appear.

tools.description: Installed catalogue recipes, keyed by recipe id.

waiting_for.description: Sign-in services the tool needs before setup can finish.

toolkits.description: The toolkits in ship.toml [toolkits], by id (contracts/toolkit.md). Absent on Ships whose tooling predates toolkits. state missing: listed, but its release folder is not there (or not root's), so nothing of it runs.

allow_root.description: Its run_as = "root" recipes may run: this release was applied with --allow-root.

overlay.description: The overlay network (phase 5). Absent or null on Ships whose tooling predates it.

joined.description: ship-ctl overlay join has succeeded and leave has not run since.

state.description: off: the overlay service is not running (never joined, or left).

name.description: The Ship's name on the overlay (e.g. ship-01.example-tailnet.ts.net).

node_id.description: The overlay's stable id for this Ship's node (Tailscale's node id), so FleetLedger can tell the Ship's device from any other with the same name. Optional: Ships whose tooling predates it leave it out.

net.description: Network visibility over the last window_h hours (phase 3); null when the Ship has no collector. The full summary is `ship-ctl net --json` (net-summary.schema.json).

new_destinations.description: Destinations (domain names, or addresses when no name is known) the Ship first contacted inside the window, newest first.

collector.description: running: ship-netwatch is recording. stopped: installed but not running. unavailable: not installed.

source.description: How connections are seen: ebpf (tcpconnect and tcplife from libbpf-tools) or ss (polling, may miss short connections).

ssh.description: SSH certificate state (phase 3). Absent from Ships older than phase 3.

host_certificate.description: The host certificate sshd presents, or null if none is installed.

principals.description: Every name the certificate is valid for.

user_ca.description: Fingerprints of the CA keys whose user certificates sshd accepts (for the agent user only).

agent_principals.description: Certificate principals that may log in as agent: agent:all, agent:tag:<tag> per Ship tag, agent:ship:<name>.

revoked_keys_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the installed revocation list, so FleetLedger can tell whether the Ship has its latest one; null if none is installed.

settings.description: What ship.toml says now, with defaults filled in: the values `ship-ctl set` manages, so FleetLedger shows a Ship's settings as the Ship has them. Optional: Ships with older tooling do not report it, and FleetLedger then shows their settings as unknown.

github.description: Optional: Ships with older tooling leave it out.

wake.description: The message to the primary agent after a boot (ship.toml [wake], defaults filled in). Optional: Ships with older tooling leave it out.

owner.description: The owner login's name, or null without one.

agent_record.description: The agent record: the Claude agents ShipShape keeps running, resumes after a boot and starts again after a crash (contracts/agent-record.schema.json, ship-ctl.md "The agent record"). Session ids are not reported. Optional: Ships with older tooling leave it out.

runtime.description: What runs the agents, e.g. herdr.

mode.description: The mode it runs in and is resumed in; null if not known.

remote_control.description: The agent record gives it Remote Control: its launches carry --remote-control while claude.remote_control is "on". The choice made with ship-ctl agent remote-control, else on for an [[autostart]] agent and off for any other. Optional: Ships with older tooling leave it out.

state.description: running: live now. starting: it should run and is not live; the next status refresh starts it (after a boot, every agent until it is resumed). failed: 3 failed tries this boot (a start that failed, or it stopped within 10 minutes of starting; attention agent-relaunch-failed). stopped: exited on purpose; an [[autostart]] agent starts afresh at the next boot, unless another agent the record keeps running works in its folder (autostart-folder-taken). unknown: the runtime is not answering.

primary.description: The Ship's primary agent (the one woken after a boot): the one marked with `ship-ctl agent primary` (marked true), else the first [[autostart]] agent the record has that should run (marked false), else null. Optional: Ships with older tooling leave it out.

last_switch.description: The last `ship-ctl runtime switch` (the one in progress, outcome in-progress). Absent on a Ship that never switched, and on Ships with older tooling.

outcome.description: As agent-record.schema.json switches[].outcome; in-progress: running now (message is its step), or stopped part way when old (attention runtime-switch-unfinished).

oneOf.description: The last boot's resume: when ship-ctl had started every recorded agent once.

errors.description: Probes that failed while building this document (non-fatal).

toolId.description: A catalogue recipe id, or toolkit/recipe for a recipe from one of your toolkits (contracts/toolkit.md).

permissionMode.description: Claude Code permission modes; "default" is the mode Claude Code calls Manual.

timestamp.description: UTC, RFC 3339, with a Z suffix.

state.description: expiring: the tool warns that the sign-in ends soon.

account.description: Signed-in account name or email as the tool reports it. FleetLedger compares it with the Ship's tag.

detail.description: e.g. plan type or method. Never a token.

scopes.description: github only: the scopes the signed-in token has, as gh auth status lists them. null or absent: not known (not signed in, a token without scopes, or older tooling).
